subject: Performance Benchmarking Review — Scheduling & Load Test Targets
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Performance Benchmarking Review — Scheduling & Load Test Targets

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time to talk through the architecture last week. Per our conversation, we'd like to run a short technical deep-dive focused specifically on performance and latency benchmarking so we can align on load-test targets and token throughput for your production workload.

Proposed agenda (30–45 mins):
- Quick architecture alignment (5–10m)
- Baseline numbers and target SLOs (10m)
- Load test plan and timeline (10m)
- Next steps and responsibilities (5m)

Slots that work for our team next week (PST):
- Tue 3/2 10:00–10:45am
- Tue 3/2 2:00–2:45pm
- Wed 3/3 9:00–9:45am

Can you confirm which time works for your engineering team? Also helpful if you can confirm the target token/sec per request and expected concurrency (e.g., 50 rps at avg 512 tokens, burst to 200 rps). I've attached a short perf-test-plan that outlines the load scenarios we typically run.

Attachments: perf-test-plan.pdf (PDF, ~120KB)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
--
Dylan Brooks
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme AI Eng <eng@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance Benchmarking Review — Scheduling & Load Test Targets

Dylan —

Thanks for the note and the plan. We're definitely interested; this is a key gating item for our rollout. Unfortunately the Tue slots are tricky for our lead infra engineer. Can we move to: Wed 3/3 11:00–11:45am PST? If that doesn't work, Thu 3/4 10:00–10:45am PST is our next-best.

For context on load: our target for initial rollout is ~60 rps steady with average 400 tokens per request, and we want to validate burst behavior to 250 rps. We're also running a smaller batch-embedding workload separately (not covered in this call).

I've looped in our eng alias so they can weigh in on availability.

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product
Acme AI

Sara —

Wed 3/3 11:00–11:45am PST works for our team. I've tentatively blocked that slot on our side.

Couple quick asks so we can come prepared and make the session productive:
- Confirm which models/variants you'll want benchmarked (open-model name + quantization if any).
- Any constraints on test environment (VPC peering needed? synthetic vs. production traffic?).
- Are there specific SLAs you need validated (p50/p95/p99 latency targets for 400 tokens)?

I'll share a short runbook & test checklist ahead of the call and bring Marcus (serving runtime lead) and Hannah (benchmarks/infra) to cover capacity and kernel-level optimizations.

Shared links: https://redwood.app/drive/perf-test-plan (perf plan)

Attachments: perf-test-plan.pdf (re-attached)

Thanks,
Dylan

Sara/Dylan —

Thanks — confirming on behalf of Redwood. Wed 3/3 11:00–11:45am PST is confirmed on our side. I've created the calendar invite and attached the .ics. Marcus and Hannah will cover the runtime baseline and capacity matrix; attached spreadsheet has our initial capacity assumptions for the scenarios you mentioned (60 rps steady / 250 rps burst at ~400 tokens).

We'll aim to cover:
- Baseline measured token/sec on our recommended configuration (quantization, batch size)
- Expected cost/throughput tradeoffs per model variant
- Load-test approach and what we'll need from you to simulate realistic traffic

Attachments: invite.ics (calendar invite), redwood-capacity-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, ~45KB)

If you want a pre-call sync with Marcus only to discuss kernel-level details, we can do a 20m slot Tue 3/2 afternoon — let us know.

–Marissa
